description: Gather context about the proposed PR

intent.problem: There is no mechanism to record every human and LLM interaction for audit and debugging purposes.
intent.goal: Log all human and LLM interactions (input and output) to a JSONL file in the .powdrr hidden directory with timestamped file names for unique CLI sessions.
intent.reasoning: A persistent file log of all interactions provides an auditable record that can be reviewed later, and using JSONL format with binary encoding ensures both text and binary content are preserved.

acceptance_criteria.description: Each log entry is a single valid JSON object on its own line in the log file.
Every interaction (input and output) is appended to the log file without overwriting previous entries.
The log file resides in the .powdrr hidden directory which is created if it does not exist.
Binary content in interactions is encoded (e.g., base64) within the JSONL entry to preserve data integrity.
The log file name includes a timestamp so each CLI session gets a unique file.

expected_tests.description: Verify that the log file contains valid JSONL with one JSON object per line.
Verify that multiple interactions are appended to the log file in order.
Verify that binary content is correctly base64-encoded in the JSONL entry and can be decoded back.
Verify that the .powdrr directory is created if it does not already exist.
Verify that the log file name includes a timestamp and different CLI sessions produce different files.

required_test_cases.description: Log a text-based human interaction and verify it appears as a valid JSONL entry.
Log an LLM output interaction and verify it appears as a valid JSONL entry.
Log an interaction containing binary content and verify it is base64-encoded in the JSONL entry.
Start with no .powdrr directory and verify it is created on first log write.
Run two CLI sessions and verify each produces a uniquely named log file with a timestamp.

expected_outcomes.description: Every human and LLM interaction (input and output) is recorded in the log file.
The log file is readable as JSONL with one JSON object per line.
Binary content is preserved through base64 encoding and can be decoded without loss.
Each CLI session produces a unique log file with a timestamped name.

non_goals.description: Log rotation or file size management is not included in this feature.
Handling concurrent writes from multiple processes is not included in this feature.
A read or query API for the log file is not included in this feature.

risks.description: Log files may grow unbounded without rotation, potentially consuming significant disk space over time.
Base64 encoding of binary content increases storage size by approximately 33 percent.
If two CLI sessions start at the exact same timestamp, they may produce the same file name.

requirements.description: Log all human and LLM interactions (input and output) to a file.
Use JSONL (JSON Lines) format for the log file.
Store the log file in a hidden .powdrr directory.
Handle both JSON and binary content in interactions.

approach.description: Append every interaction to the log file as a new line.
Encode each interaction as a single JSON object per line in the log file.
Encode binary content within JSONL entries to preserve data integrity.

entities.summary: A single interaction record containing timestamp, role, and content (input or output) from human or LLM interactions.

invariants.description: Each log entry must be a single valid JSON object on its own line in the log file.
Binary content in interactions must be encoded (e.g., base64) within the JSONL entry to preserve data integrity.
The log file must reside in the .powdrr hidden directory.

guidance.description: Writes to the log file should be append-only to prevent data corruption and ensure every interaction is recorded.
The .powdrr directory should be created if it does not already exist when writing the first log entry.

entities.rationale: Cites "log-interactions" and "append-interactions" - every interaction input and output must be logged as a discrete entry.

features.description: Log all human and LLM interactions (input and output) to a file.
functional_requirements: Each log entry must be a single valid JSON object on its own line in the log file.
Binary content in interactions must be encoded (e.g., base64) within the JSONL entry to preserve data integrity.
The log file must reside in the .powdrr hidden directory.
Writes to the log file should be append-only to prevent data corruption and ensure every interaction is recorded.
The .powdrr directory should be created if it does not already exist when writing the first log entry.
Append a timestamp to the file name to make each CLI session get a unique file.

decisions.description: Ensure JSON and binary field work.
